2. Short facts leading to this Rule are that on 17-7-1997 the opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 96 of 1997 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court, Chittagong impleading the petitioners as defendants for recovery of khas possession by evicting the defendants from the suit land declaring them as their (plaintiffs) permissive possessor and also for declaration that the BS Khatian relating to suit land is illegal, incorrect, void, inoperative and not binding upon them. 

 6. In course of trial the plaintiffs examined three witnesses namely PW 1, Sunil Chandra Sarker who proved the notice dated 10-4-1997 as Exhibit 1, PW 2, Anil Majumder and PW 3 Kabir Ahmed, were examined to corroborate the PW 1. The defendants examined five witnesses to prove their case, of them DW 1 Chandan Sen proved RS khatian No. 881, BS khatian No. 1695 and kabala deed dated 12-3-1932 as Exhibits T, T-1 and U respectively. DW 2, Rabindra Lal Sen, DW 3, Bulbul Sen and DW 4 Badal Chowdhury, DW 5 Sheik Md Shahjahan were examined to corroborate the evidence of DW 1. 

 17. On going to the materials on record it transpires that the suit land comprising three plots viz plot Nos. 5233, 5238, and 5239 had originally belonged to Matanga Sundari. The plaintiffs claimed that they as heirs inherited the suit land and the defendants are the permissive possessors under them. The defendants claimed that their predecessor purchased 11 decimals of land from plot Nos. 5233 and 5238 from Matanga Sundari by registered kabala deed dated 12-3-1932 (Exhibit ক). It further transpires RS khatian No. 881 (Exhibit and BS khatian No. 1695 (Exhibit ক-১) comprises three plots being plot Nos. 5233, 5238, 5239. The plaintiffs examined three witnesses in support of their claim, of them PW 1 Sunil Chandra Sarker plaintiff No. 1 himself testified that the defendants are the permissive possessors under them but he failed to disclose any specific date as to when and how the defendants entered into the suit land as permissive possessors. Moreso, the notice dated 10-4-1997 (Exhibit 1) served upon the defendants does not disclose any such date. The defendants examined five witnesses, of them DW 1 Chandon Sen categorically stated that their predecessor purchased 11 decimals of land from plot Nos. 5233 and 5238 vide kabala deed dated 12-3-1932 (Exhibit ক) and they as heirs are enjoying and possessing the same. His evidence furnished corroboration with other evidence. The evidence of all the DWs are uniform, consistent and corroborative with each other. There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve those competent witnesses whatsoever, so the same are invulnerable to the credibility. 

 18. It further transpires that there is absolutely no evidence that the suit homestead measuring an area “বাঁশের বেড়া ও টিনের ছাউনি যুক্ত দোচালা গৃহ যাহা উত্তর দক্ষিণ ১২ হাত ও পূর্ব পশ্চিম ৭হাত এবং তৎসংলগ্ন বাঁশের বেড়া ছনের ছাউনি যুক্ত চৌচালা বিশিষ্ট গৃহ যাহা উত্তর দক্ষিণ ১২হাত পূর্ব পশ্চিম ৫হাত” situated upon plot No. 5239. The schedule of the plaint comprises three plots being plot Nos. 5233, 5238, and 5237. It has been proved by evidence that RS khatian No. 881 (Exhibit comprises those three plots and the predecessor of the defendants purchased 11 decimals of land from plot Nos. 5233, 5238 and they as heirs have been possessing those plots which are inclusive of the suit land. Admittedly there is no partition. Upon consideration of the aforesaid documents. I am of the view that the defendants are the co-sharers of the suit land and they are in exclusive possession in the specific land, so they are entitled to retain the same until partition. 

 19. It will be pertinent to mention that the learned Counsel once again gave emphasis that on 25-3-1998 the plaintiff filed application for amendment of the plaint deleting plot Nos. 5233 and 5238, so according to him the defendants are in permissive possession in plot No. 5239. But from the materials on record I find that although the plaintiffs filed application for such amendment but the same was not allowed by an express order of the trial Court. It is evident from the evidence on record, that the plaintiffs hopelessly failed to prove that the defendants are their permissive possessor in the suit land and both the Courts below failed to appreciate the documentary evidence of the defendants, particularly RS Khatian No. 881 (Exhibit ক) and registered kabala deed dated 12-3-1932 (Exhibit খ). Therefore, I hold that the judgments of the Courts below are based on misreading and non consideration of the material evidence on record affecting the merit of the case.
